claims.claim: Tomlinson says the reader can rely on Le Guin explaining a noted difference in due course rather than at once.
claims.quote: rely on her explaining that difference in due course

claims.claim: Tomlinson quotes the opening of The Dispossessed, which describes the wall as built of uncut rocks roughly mortared.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin (The Dispossessed), quoted by Rob Tomlinson
claims.quote: It was built of uncut rocks roughly mortared

claims.claim: Tomlinson says Le Guin depicts the under-belly of a dazzling society in just a few pages of dense, carefully-worked text.
claims.quote: In just a few pages of dense, carefully-worked text

claims.claim: Tomlinson renders the poor quarter of Nio as broken street lights, shuttered windows and shop fronts gutted by fire.
claims.source: Rob Tomlinson, A Good Read (rob-tomlinson.com), paraphrasing The Dispossessed
claims.quote: Street lights were broken, windows shuttered, shop fronts gutted by fire

claims.claim: Theodora Goss reads the opening of A Wizard of Earthsea as a camera that swoops down over the island from its high peak.
claims.source: Theodora Goss, "Stonecoast: Wizard of Earthsea", theodoragoss.com, 28 February 2015
claims.quote: we swoop down over the island, from its high peak

claims.claim: Goss says the opening moves from a grander, larger view toward a smaller, more intimate one.
claims.quote: moves from a grander, larger view toward a smaller, more intimate

claims.claim: Goss notes the opening names its subject in descending order, Sparrowhawk to Ged to Duny.
Goss argues the opening scene is structured by oppositions between boy and man, village and world.
claims.quote: structured by the oppositions between boy and man, village and world

claims.claim: Doug Merrill observes that no people appear in the first paragraph of The Dispossessed.
claims.source: Doug Merrill, "The Dispossessed by Ursula K. Le Guin", The Frumious Consortium, 19 March 2018
claims.quote: No people appear in the first paragraph

claims.claim: Merrill notes no names are mentioned in the novel until the seventh page.
claims.source: Doug Merrill, The Frumious Consortium, 19 March 2018
claims.quote: no names are mentioned until the seventh

claims.claim: Merrill says the opening paragraph establishes the rough and improvised nature of a key setting.
claims.source: Doug Merrill, The Frumious Consortium, 19 March 2018
claims.quote: the rough and improvised nature of a key setting

claims.claim: Merrill lists among the opening paragraph's subjects things that do not look important but are.
claims.source: Doug Merrill, The Frumious Consortium, 19 March 2018
claims.quote: things that do not look important but are

claims.claim: Merrill says Le Guin's sketches of incidental characters hint at full lives lived off the page.
claims.source: Doug Merrill, The Frumious Consortium, 19 March 2018
claims.quote: hint at the full lives they have lived off the page

claims.claim: A Cannonball Read reviewer calls Le Guin's writing spare and lyrical, begging to be read aloud.
claims.source: alannaofdoom, "Bright the hawk's flight on the empty sky", Cannonball Read, 13 February 2014
claims.quote: Her writing is spare and lyrical, just begging to be read aloud

claims.claim: The same reviewer says the first lines have the feel of an old legend told and retold around hearth fires.
claims.quote: the feel of an old legend, told and retold around hearth
